lessons.title: One Pour

play.shortDesc: Two colours, three bottles, one pour
play.targetObjective: Pour so every bottle holds one colour.
stepByStep: Tap the bottle you want to pour from.
Tap the bottle to pour into.
A colour only goes onto the same colour, or into an empty bottle.
play.kidTip: Look for the two bottles that share a colour.
play.audioPrompt: Pour the colours together. One pour finishes this rack.

lessons.pedagogyTip: One move isolates the rule before any planning is asked for.

lessons.title: Two Pours

play.shortDesc: The same rule, twice over
play.targetObjective: Pour so every bottle holds one colour.
stepByStep: Find a colour sitting on top of another.
Pour it onto its match.
Do the same again.
play.kidTip: Only the top colour ever moves.
play.audioPrompt: Two pours this time. Move each colour onto its match.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A second repetition before anything new is introduced.

lessons.title: Use the Empty Bottle

play.shortDesc: The spare bottle is the only way through
play.targetObjective: Use the empty bottle to unstack the colours.
stepByStep: Find a colour with nowhere to go.
Pour it into the empty bottle.
Now the colour underneath can move.
play.kidTip: An empty bottle takes any colour.
play.audioPrompt: There is one empty bottle. It will take any colour you need to move.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The empty bottle is the first tool, and the first thing worth spending carefully.

lessons.title: The Whole Run Moves

play.shortDesc: Matching colours travel as one
play.targetObjective: Move a run of the same colour in a single pour.
stepByStep: Find two or three of the same colour stacked together.
Pour them onto their match.
They all move at once, if there is room.
play.kidTip: Three the same is still one pour.
play.audioPrompt: Colours that are stacked together move as one. Watch how many travel.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Naming the whole-run rule stops a child counting pours one segment at a time.

lessons.title: Sort Three Colours

play.shortDesc: The first rack that needs a plan
play.targetObjective: Sort all three colours into their own bottles.
stepByStep: Look at the whole rack before pouring.
Decide which bottle you can empty first.
Pour, then look again.
play.kidTip: Think about which bottle you want to empty, not just which pour is possible.
play.audioPrompt: Three colours now. Look at the whole rack before you pour.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The first rack where a legal pour is not automatically a good one.

lessons.title: Short and Tall

play.shortDesc: Bottles that hold three, four or five
play.targetObjective: Sort the rack when the bottles are different sizes.
stepByStep: Look at how tall each bottle is.
A short bottle fills sooner than a tall one.
Check there is room before you pour.
play.kidTip: A taller bottle holds more. Count the space, not the bottles.
play.audioPrompt: These bottles are different sizes. Check how much room there is before you pour.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Capacity becomes a thing to read rather than assume once it stops being uniform.

lessons.title: Will It Fit?

play.shortDesc: The colours match, but the room does not
play.targetObjective: Find the pours that actually fit.
stepByStep: Find a colour sitting on its match.
Count the empty space in the bottle below it.
If it will not all fit, look for another pour.
play.kidTip: Matching colours is not enough. There has to be room.
play.audioPrompt: Sometimes the colours match but there is not enough room. Count the space first.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Separating 'legal colour' from 'enough room' is the first two-part condition in the skill.

lessons.title: Fill It to the Top

play.shortDesc: A bottle is only finished when it is full
play.targetObjective: Fill each bottle exactly to the top with one colour.
stepByStep: Pick a colour to collect.
Bring every part of it into one bottle.
The bottle is done when it is full and one colour.
play.kidTip: Half a bottle of one colour is not finished yet.
play.audioPrompt: A bottle is finished when it is full and holds one colour. Fill each one to the top.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Naming the finish condition stops a child stopping at a tidy-looking half-bottle.

lessons.title: Count Before You Pour

play.shortDesc: See how many will travel before you commit
play.targetObjective: Know how many segments a pour will move.
stepByStep: Tap a bottle to pick it up.
The number shows how many will pour.
Check they will all fit before you tap the next bottle.
play.kidTip: The number on the bottle is how many are about to move.
play.audioPrompt: When you pick a bottle up, the number tells you how many will pour.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Turning the run length from something noticed into something read makes the whole-run rule usable.

lessons.title: Practice: Pouring

play.shortDesc: Five racks across everything so far
play.targetObjective: Sort five racks without help.
stepByStep: Look at the whole rack first.
Decide which bottle to empty.
Pour, then look again.
play.kidTip: No hints here. Take your time.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Practice measures pace across the taught techniques, so it draws from all of them rather than one.

lessons.title: Four Colours

play.shortDesc: A fourth colour joins the rack
play.targetObjective: Sort all four colours into their own bottles.
stepByStep: Look at the whole rack before pouring.
Decide which bottle you can empty first.
Pour, then look again.
play.kidTip: One more colour means one more thing to keep track of. Empty a bottle before you fill one.
play.audioPrompt: Four colours now. Keep one bottle free if you can.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The first rack where holding the whole plan in mind matters more than the next legal pour.

lessons.title: Taller Bottles

play.shortDesc: Five deep instead of four
play.targetObjective: Sort all four colours into the taller bottles.
stepByStep: Check how deep each bottle is.
A taller bottle takes a longer run.
Pour, then look again.
play.kidTip: These bottles hold five. A run of five can move in one pour.
play.audioPrompt: Taller bottles. They hold five now, not four.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Capacity and colour count grow separately, so the child meets one new thing at a time.

lessons.title: One Space Left

play.shortDesc: Only one free slot in the whole rack
play.targetObjective: Sort every colour with only one space to work in.
stepByStep: Find the only free space.
Ask what has to move into it first.
Pour, then look again.
play.kidTip: There is only one space. Spend it on the pour that frees another.
play.audioPrompt: Only one space left. Choose what goes into it carefully.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A single free slot forces the child to sequence rather than search.

lessons.title: No Free Bottle

play.shortDesc: Nothing starts empty
play.targetObjective: Make your own space, then sort every colour.
stepByStep: No bottle starts empty.
Find a pour that empties one.
Then use the space you made.
play.kidTip: You have to make space before you can use it. Look for a bottle that is nearly one colour already.
play.audioPrompt: No empty bottle this time. Make one.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Space becomes something the child creates rather than something the rack provides.

lessons.title: The Locked Bottle

play.shortDesc: One bottle is corked until another is done
play.targetObjective: Finish the right bottle first to open the corked one.
stepByStep: Find the corked bottle.
See which bottle it is waiting on.
Finish that one first.
play.kidTip: The cork comes off when the bottle it waits on holds one colour. Work out which one that is.
play.audioPrompt: One bottle is corked. Finish the bottle it is waiting on.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The first lesson where the order of two correct pours is what matters.

lessons.title: Two Locks

play.shortDesc: A cork that opens another cork
play.targetObjective: Work out the order that opens every bottle.
stepByStep: Find the bottle that is not waiting on anything.
Finish it to open the next.
Follow the chain.
play.kidTip: One cork opens another. Start with the bottle that is not waiting on anything.
play.audioPrompt: Two corks now. Find the one you can open first.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A chain of dependencies, which is planning two steps rather than one.

lessons.title: The One-Way Bottle

play.shortDesc: One bottle takes liquid and never gives it back
play.targetObjective: Sort every colour without trapping anything in the one-way bottle.
stepByStep: Find the one-way bottle.
Anything poured in stays in.
Only pour the colour that belongs there.
play.kidTip: Liquid goes into that bottle and never comes out. Be sure before you pour.
play.audioPrompt: One bottle only receives. Whatever goes in stays in.

lessons.pedagogyTip: An irreversible move makes the child check a plan before committing to it.

lessons.title: Think Before You Pour

play.shortDesc: A pour budget, with a little room
play.targetObjective: Sort the rack within the pours you are given.
stepByStep: Count the pours you have.
Plan before the first one.
Undo costs you nothing.
play.kidTip: You have a couple of spare pours. Plan first and you will not need them.
play.audioPrompt: Watch your pours this time. You do not have many.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A budget converts 'a legal pour' into 'a pour worth making'.

lessons.title: The Shortest Way

play.shortDesc: Exactly the shortest solution, no spare pours
play.targetObjective: Sort the rack in the fewest pours there are.
stepByStep: There are no spare pours.
Work the whole plan out first.
Undo and start over cost nothing.
play.kidTip: Every pour has to count. Work it out before you start.
play.audioPrompt: The shortest way only. Every pour has to count.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The tightest constraint in the skill, and the reason undo is free.

lessons.title: Practice: Planning

play.shortDesc: Five racks across every planning technique
play.targetObjective: Sort five racks without help.
stepByStep: Look at the whole rack first.
Corks, one-way bottles and budgets all still apply.
Pour, then look again.
play.kidTip: No hints here. Take your time.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Practice measures pace across the taught techniques, so it draws from all of them rather than one.

lessons.title: What Is Underneath

play.shortDesc: Two colours in each bottle are covered
play.targetObjective: Sort the rack without knowing everything at the start.
stepByStep: The covered segments show a question mark.
You can always see the colour on top.
Pour, and what was underneath comes into view.
play.kidTip: You cannot see the bottom yet. Work with the colours you can see, and find out the rest.
play.audioPrompt: Some colours are covered. You can always see the top one.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The first rack that cannot be solved by looking; the child has to act to learn.

lessons.title: Reveal As You Go

play.shortDesc: Four colours, and most of them covered
play.targetObjective: Uncover the rack as you sort it.
stepByStep: Pour to find out what is underneath.
A plan made before you look may need changing.
Undo costs nothing if a colour surprises you.
play.kidTip: Your first plan is a guess. Change it when a new colour appears.
play.audioPrompt: Four colours, mostly covered. Pour to find out what is underneath.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Planning under uncertainty: the point is revising the plan, not having the right one first.

lessons.title: Guess the Result

play.shortDesc: Say what one pour will do, before it happens
play.targetObjective: Choose the rack that the pour will make.
stepByStep: Read the rack you are given.
Find the run on top of the pouring bottle.
Count the room in the bottle it pours into.
play.kidTip: The whole run of one colour moves together, as long as there is room for it.
play.audioPrompt: Look before you pour. Which rack comes next?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Doing and predicting are different skills; a child can sort by trial and error and still not say what a pour will do.

lessons.title: Guess Two Ahead

play.shortDesc: Two pours to hold in your head
play.targetObjective: Choose the rack that both pours will make.
stepByStep: Work out the first pour.
Then work out the second on what the first leaves.
Choose the rack that matches.
play.kidTip: Do the first pour in your head, then the second on top of it.
play.audioPrompt: Two pours this time. Picture the first, then the second.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Holding an imagined state and acting on it again is where planning becomes reasoning.
